comments.note: A07 — Authentication Failures (Low). File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/PasswordSetupViewModel.cs. No minimum password length or complexity policy is enforced. CanSubmit requires only Password.Length > 0 and equality with Confirm, meaning a single-character password is accepted. For a local single-user desktop app this is an acceptable design choice. Recommended: add a configurable minimum length constant (e.g., 8 characters) if the threat model changes or if the app is shared among multiple users.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures (Info). Files: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/PasswordSetupViewModel.cs. Same as WP-013: Password and Confirm strings are not zero-wiped from the heap (inherent .NET limitation). Both are set to string.Empty before the async delegate call, which is the correct defensive pattern for minimising in-memory exposure window.

Positive findings: CanSubmit uses StringComparison.Ordinal (correct, case-sensitive). Both Password and Confirm fields use PasswordChar='\u25cf' in PasswordSetupView.axaml. Both fields are cleared before the delegate call (lines 46-48). No business logic in view code-behind. All security-positive patterns present.

comments.note: No blocking or Fix-Forward findings. PasswordSetupViewModel is consistent with the LogonViewModel pattern. CanSubmit correctly combines Length > 0 guards with Ordinal equality — the length checks are essential because string.Equals("", "", Ordinal) is true, so removing them would allow an all-empty submission. Three-way AC-1 test decomposition (empty-password, empty-confirm, mismatch) gives precise coverage. Eager-clear before delegate call is correct and consistent with WP-013.
